newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Aug 15.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.
* Sealed Air agreed to buy the packaging lines of W.R. Grace in a $4.9 billion tax-free stock and cash deal.
* United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union resumed contract talks, although neither side would predict when the strike might end.
* Travelers Group named pension fund executive Thomas Jones to run its Smith Barney Asset Management unit.
* Delta Air is expected to name Unicom vice chairman Leo Mullin as president and CEO.
* Healthsouth offered to buy large chunks of Columbia/HCA, after failing to receive a response to an offer to buy the hospital for up to $45 a share.
* Columbia/HCA confirmed that two executives allied with ousted CEO Scott resigned.
* The consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in July, while industrial production grew at a 0.2 percent pace.
* Bonds rallied, although stocks posted only moderate gains, with the Dow Industrials closing up 13.71 to 7842.03.
* Tobacco officials are balking at changes the White House is considering to strengthen the proposed pact with the industry.
* PepsiCo unveiled details of the planned spinoff of its fast-food operations.
* Fund manager Tom Marsico's departure from Janus came after he had talks with his boss about jointly acquiring the company.
* Reader's Digest hired an executive search firm to help it find a new CEO.
* Indonesia removed the nation's rupiah's restricted trading band.
* New York's Tisch family recorded $467.4 million in gross investment losses in the second quarter.
